high.title: TSMC's 2nm Process: Google Breaks Apple's First-Mover Tradition — Pixel 11 to Launch in August
high.summary: TSMC's (2330) 2nm process node has entered mass production, igniting a smartphone chip race. In a notable break from tradition, Google — not Apple — will be the first to market with a 2nm-powered device. Google's "Made by Google" event is scheduled for August 12, where it is expected to unveil the Pixel 11 series featuring the in-house Tensor G6 chip, fabricated on TSMC's 2nm process. This marks the first time Apple has not led a new TSMC node launch in recent memory. Apple's iPhone 18 series is expected roughly one month later, with MediaTek (2454) and Qualcomm flagship 2nm chips following in September or beyond. Industry observers note that regardless of which OEM launches first, TSMC is the ultimate beneficiary as 2nm adoption across flagship smartphones becomes mainstream. This development reinforces TSMC's pricing power, technological moat, and multi-customer dependency reduction — all positive signals for the stock ahead of its earnings call on July 16.

high.title: TSMC Price Hike Wave Spreads to Mature Nodes — First Increase in Over Three Years
high.summary: TSMC (2330) is reportedly notifying IC design customers of price increases on mature process nodes, effective January next year — its first mature-node price hike in over three years since the COVID-era increases. Multiple IC design firms confirmed receipt of notices, with individual customer hike magnitudes varying; industry estimates suggest low single-digit percentage increases, to be finalized in Q4. This follows a string of advanced node price hikes and signals that AI-driven semiconductor demand has now cascaded from GPUs and HPC chips all the way down to peripheral components such as power management ICs (PMICs). TSMC enters its earnings call (July 16) in a silent period and declined to comment. The development is highly significant: it demonstrates broad-based pricing power across TSMC's entire product spectrum, supports a structurally higher revenue trajectory, and is likely to prompt upward revisions to consensus estimates. Market implications are strongly positive for TSMC's margin outlook and for the broader Taiwan semiconductor supply chain.

high.title: TSMC Price Hike Effect Ripples to Mature Foundries — UMC, PSMC, Vanguard to Follow with Larger Increases
high.summary: Following TSMC's (2330) decision to raise mature-node pricing, pure-play mature foundries UMC (2303), PSMC (6770), and Vanguard International Semiconductor (5347) are expected to implement their own — likely larger — price increases. Industry sources indicate UMC issued a fresh pricing notice to customers earlier this month, citing rising raw material costs and Singapore fab expansion expenses, with selective hikes on new processes and new orders; a comprehensive pricing renegotiation with all customers is planned for next year. PSMC's president noted that prior price hike effects have been reflected in revenues since June, driving significant H2 revenue growth, and that this memory upcycle may be more aggressive than the COVID-era surge. Vanguard's chairman confirmed the company had already announced and received customer acceptance of its own price hike measures. The sector-wide repricing event is a material positive catalyst for UMC, PSMC, and Vanguard, supporting H2 earnings upgrades across mature-node foundry names. Investors should monitor Q3 guidance from these companies closely.

high.title: Hon Hai, Quanta, Wistron Order Momentum Strengthens as AI Model Upgrades Accelerate Computing Demand
high.summary: OpenAI, Google, and SpaceX have each launched new AI models in July targeting enterprise and consumer markets, triggering a surge in AI computing demand. Institutional investors are bullish that this acceleration will sustain strong AI server order momentum for Hon Hai (2317), Quanta (2382), Wistron (3231), Inventec (2356), and Compal (2324) through 2028. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol flagship model has set new benchmarks across coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and scientific domains, outperforming Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 in key evaluations. Google is reportedly preparing to launch its Gemini 3 model mid-month. For fund managers, this represents a sustained structural demand driver for Taiwan's AI server supply chain. Hon Hai in particular warrants close attention given its diversified AI server exposure. The competitive intensity among frontier AI labs suggests capex cycles from North American cloud service providers (CSPs) remain robust, providing multi-year revenue visibility for Taiwan ODM manufacturers.

high.title: AI Server Opportunity Accelerates — ODM Manufacturers Launch Global Capacity Expansion
high.summary: Taiwan's major ODM manufacturers — Hon Hai (2317), Quanta (2382), and Wistron (3231) — are aggressively expanding global AI server production capacity as North American CSP capital expenditures hit record highs. Industry sources indicate that new AI server capacity for H2 2026 and full-year 2027 is nearly fully booked, creating a highly visible order backlog. Hon Hai is building capacity across the US, Mexico, and Taiwan targeting L6–L11 AI server tiers. Quanta is constructing three new US facilities (California and Tennessee) expected to be operational by year-end, with AI server capacity projected to double year-over-year. Wistron, in partnership with subsidiary Wiwynn (6669), is developing R&D and testing centers in Zhubei and Kaohsiung while building L10/L11 capacity in Southeast Asia and North America under a localized delivery model, having secured multiple new CSP development contracts. With Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon, and Oracle all driving demand, this article confirms that Taiwan's AI server supply chain is entering a multi-year capacity supercycle. This is highly material for investors holding Hon Hai, Quanta, and Wistron positions.

high.title: TSMC June Revenue Hits Record Highs — Three Major Milestones; H1 2026 Revenue Breaks NT$2 Trillion for First Time
high.summary:
TSMC (2330) reported June consolidated revenue of NT$442.68 billion, setting a new single-month record for the second consecutive month — up 6.2% MoM and a striking 67.9% YoY. Q2 2026 consolidated revenue reached NT$1.27 trillion, a new quarterly high (+12.02% QoQ, +36.05% YoY). Most significantly, H1 2026 revenue crossed the NT$2 trillion threshold for the first time ever, reaching NT$2.4 trillion — a new all-time record for the first half of any year (+35.6% YoY).

The strong performance is primarily attributed to surging AI and high-performance computing (HPC) orders driving advanced node utilization. Q2 revenue came in near the upper bound of TSMC's own April guidance of USD 39–40.2 billion (assuming TWD/USD at 31.7). Actual USD revenue and gross margin figures will be officially confirmed at the Thursday (July 16) earnings call.

**Market Implications:** This revenue beat sets a highly constructive tone ahead of the earnings call. Institutional investors are likely to further revise EPS and target price estimates upward. With H2 also expected to benefit from Apple new product cycles and continued AI demand, TSMC remains the key bellwether for Taiwan's broader technology sector. The stock closed at NT$2,440 (+NT$25) on July 13, though foreign investors were net sellers of 2,045 lots and ADR slipped ~1% in early Monday trading — suggesting some near-term profit-taking despite the strong fundamentals.

high.title: Lite-On Invests NT$30 Billion in U.S. to Capture AI Infrastructure and Energy Growth Opportunities
high.summary: Lite-On Technology (2301), a major power supply manufacturer, announced a USD $919 million (approximately NT$30 billion) investment to establish a new production facility in McKinney, Texas. This investment targets rapidly growing demand in AI infrastructure and energy transition markets. Lite-On already raised its 2026 capex guidance by 18% (from NT$11 billion to NT$13 billion) at a recent analyst day — notably, this new U.S. facility investment is on top of that revised figure. Analysts expect Lite-On to raise its capex guidance a second time this year, underscoring the robustness of AI-driven demand. The new Texas facility complements the existing Plano, Texas plant, which has six production lines focused on Battery Backup Units (BBU) but is operating beyond capacity. Chairman Steve Sung framed the investment as a key milestone in Lite-On's global growth strategy, strengthening North American manufacturing presence and enabling end-to-end local service delivery. **Market Implication:** This signals intensifying capital commitment among Taiwan's AI supply chain players into U.S. manufacturing. Investors should watch for a second capex revision and monitor margin impacts from accelerated spend. Lit-On's local supply chain partners could also benefit.

high.title: Power Supply Duopoly Expands Capacity to Strengthen AI Ecosystem
high.summary: Both Lite-On (2301) and Delta Electronics (2308) are aggressively expanding production capacity to meet surging AI data center demand over the next two to three years. Delta Electronics broke the NT$400 billion capex barrier in 2025, reaching NT$46.1 billion, with 2026 capex expected to exceed NT$50 billion, driven by tight capacity at its Thailand and U.S. facilities. Lite-On's strategy emphasizes ecosystem building over vertical integration — partnering with cooperative suppliers to offer end-to-end U.S. local services for cloud service providers (CSPs). **Market Implication:** The combined capex surge from Taiwan's power supply leaders reflects a structural, multi-year AI infrastructure investment cycle. For fund managers, both stocks represent direct AI infrastructure beneficiaries; supply chain partners of Lite-On and Delta may also see incremental order flow as the two seek to localize their ecosystems in the U.S.

high.title: Foreign Investors Drop Bombshell: ABF Substrate "Epic Shortage" — Target Prices for Taiwan Firms Double
high.summary: Goldman Sachs released a major Asia Technology Industry report flagging a severe and worsening ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) substrate shortage, projecting that Taiwan's key PCB/substrate supply chain will deliver earnings significantly above consensus through 2027–2028. The bank dramatically raised target prices on four Taiwan-listed names: Nanya PCB (8046) upgraded to "Buy" and top pick with target doubled from NT$1,115 to NT$2,310; Tripod (3189) "Buy" with target raised from NT$555 to NT$1,120; Unimicron (3037) "Neutral" with target from NT$630 to NT$1,140; and Zhen Ding (4958) "Buy" with target from NT$388 to NT$824. Lead times have already stretched from 3–4 months at start of 2026 to 12 months currently. Goldman analyst estimates the shortage will persist for over 30 months, with shortage rates reaching 14%, 34%, and 51% in H2 2026, 2027, and 2028 respectively, driven by surging AI ASIC substrate demand and stronger-than-expected server CPU substrate orders. This implies accelerating pricing power and meaningful gross margin upside for Taiwan substrate makers. Fund managers with exposure to AI infrastructure supply chains should treat this as a high-conviction signal to review positioning in this space.

high.title: US-Iran Military Conflict Resumes — Wall Street Closes Lower, Semiconductor Index Plunges 4.78%
high.summary: A renewed round of US-Iran military conflict rattled global markets, sending all four major US indices lower at Monday's close. The Dow Jones fell 0.26% to 52,498, the S&P 500 declined 0.79% to 7,515, the Nasdaq dropped 1.55% to 25,873, and — most critically for Taiwan-focused investors — the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) plummeted 4.78% to 12,347. This sharp SOX decline is a direct negative leading indicator for Taiwan's semiconductor sector, which includes TSMC, MediaTek, and the broader AI chip supply chain. Geopolitical risk premium is rising, and any escalation in the Middle East could further suppress risk appetite. Taiwan equity markets, particularly tech-heavy names, should be expected to open under pressure. Fund managers should monitor oil price movements and any further geopolitical developments closely, as sustained conflict could weigh on global growth expectations and tech valuations.

high.title: Foreign Investors Continue Net Selling Taiwan Stocks; Domestic Funds Hold the Line — U.S. CPI, Futures Settlement, and TSMC Earnings Call Are This Week's Key Pivots
high.summary: Foreign investors extended their net selling streak to seven consecutive sessions on July 13, offloading a net NT$19.55 billion in Taiwan equities, bringing total July net sales to approximately NT$319.45 billion. The persistent selling pressure is attributed largely to recent TWD weakness against the USD, which reduces the FX-adjusted return on Taiwan equity holdings for foreign institutional investors. Despite an intraday surge of 976 points at the open, the TAIEX reversed to near-flat by close, with domestic investment trusts (投信) providing the key buffer. Market strategists from Fubon Investment Advisory and Chung Hwa Investment Advisory maintain a constructive medium-term view, anchored by TSMC's record monthly revenue of NT$442.68 billion — hitting the high end of its own guidance — and continued AI supply chain momentum. Three near-term catalysts to watch this week: (1) U.S. CPI print, (2) Taiwan futures index settlement, and (3) TSMC's earnings call. Tactically, analysts caution against the index breaching the recent black-candle low of 44,594 points. Sector rotation remains rapid; financial stocks, defense, and biotech are flagged as short-term plays, while AI-themed stocks remain the structural long.

high.title: Listed Companies' June Revenue Kings Revealed: Hon Hai Holds "Volume Crown," AI and Semiconductor Supply Chain Drive Outperformance
high.summary: Full June and H1 2026 revenue figures for all listed and OTC companies were released on July 13. The top revenue generators continue to be dominated by AI and technology heavyweights: Hon Hai (2317) led with NT$821.76 billion in June revenue, retaining the "volume crown," followed by TSMC at NT$442.68 billion and Quanta Computer at NT$385.19 billion. These figures underscore the sustained strength of the AI server and semiconductor supply chain. Among mid- and small-caps, construction firm Lianshang (4113) claimed the "month-on-month growth crown" with an extraordinary 2,023x MoM surge driven by concentrated project completions. Semiconductor automation integrator Zhushan Technology (6739) led the "consecutive growth" category with 25 straight months of revenue increases, reflecting robust semiconductor capex and production line upgrade cycles. For fund managers, the data reinforces the dominance of AI infrastructure names as core long positions and validates the ongoing capex supercycle narrative heading into Q2 earnings season.

medium.title: US-China Robotics Race Drives New Component Restocking Cycle — Taiwan Supply Chain Beneficiaries Include Meilink, Ability Opto, and Solomon
medium.summary: The intensifying US-China competition in humanoid robotics is generating a fresh component procurement wave benefiting Taiwan's supply chain. On the US side, Tesla is reportedly accelerating Optimus Gen-3 mass production, targeting 1,000 units per week by September and doubling to 2,000–2,500 units by year-end, with confirmed August orders already placed. This benefits Taiwan suppliers Meilink (2464) and Ability Opto-Electronics (3019). On the Chinese side, Unitree Robotics is pursuing an IPO and expanding its product pipeline, supporting Solomon (part of the supply chain) and Hiwin Technologies (2049). Institutional investors view the Physical AI era as a structural demand driver for lenses, joints, and precision components, positioning Taiwan's robotics supply chain for multi-quarter tailwinds.

medium.title: Aviation Duo EVA Air and China Airlines Poised for Q4 Freight Rate Peak Amid AI Cargo Surge
medium.summary: AI infrastructure buildout is driving exceptional demand for air cargo, particularly on Asia-to-North America routes, with IATA reporting a ~20% YoY volume increase on that lane in May — nearly triple the global average of 6%. Spot rates on Asia-Pacific to North America routes surged 36% YoY in June per Xeneta. EVA Air (2618) posted June freight revenue of NT$6.65 billion (+48.3% YoY) and China Airlines (2610) reported NT$8.09 billion (+51.6% YoY). Both carriers expect Q3 capacity to remain tight, with Q4 rates potentially reaching new highs as AI chip/server shipments, back-to-school, and holiday stocking converge. This is a positive near-term catalyst for both aviation names, though investors should monitor any trade policy or demand normalization risks.

medium.title: "Greater South New Silicon Valley" Initiative Takes Effect — Semiconductor Cluster Footprint Gradually Shifts Southward
medium.summary: Taiwan's semiconductor industry is experiencing a meaningful geographic shift southward, with 96 factories now operating in Tainan, Kaohsiung, and Pingtung — accounting for over 20% of the total, up 6 percentage points over the past decade. President Lai Ching-te's "Balanced Taiwan" policy and the government's "Greater South New Silicon Valley" initiative are accelerating this transition, positioning southern Taiwan as a counterpart to the established "Hsinchu-Taoyuan-Miaoli Silicon Valley." TSMC (2330) is central to this shift, with 6 of its 16 planned wafer and advanced packaging facilities located in Tainan and Kaohsiung, and 4 more in Chiayi, forming a semiconductor "S-corridor." For investors, this trend signals sustained infrastructure investment and supply chain development opportunities in southern Taiwan, while reinforcing TSMC's long-term domestic capacity expansion strategy. Note that approximately 75% of electronics factories remain concentrated in northern Taiwan, indicating this is a gradual, long-term structural shift rather than an immediate dislocation.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Set for Catch-Up Rally; TSMC Earnings Call Pre-Positioning Targets 48,000 Index Level
medium.summary: Taiwan's equity market was closed for Typhoon Bawei, but during the holiday period U.S. equities surged with Meta and AMD posting strong gains, while Japanese and Korean markets rallied over 1%. MediaTek (2454) reported above-estimate quarterly revenue and Nanya Technology (2408) delivered a positive earnings call, further bolstering bullish sentiment. Analysts at Fubon Investment and Yongfeng Investment cited these as favorable conditions for a catch-up rally upon market reopening. With TSMC's July 16 earnings call acting as the near-term catalyst, positioning ahead of the event is expected to push the TAIEX toward the 48,000 level. TSMC's Q2 EPS is forecast at NT$25–26, with the most optimistic projections at NT$28–29, potentially implying H1 EPS of ~NT$50 (equivalent to earning five times the par value of capital in six months). Q3 revenue is forecast to grow ~12% QoQ with gross margin potentially breaching 70%.

medium.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Signals Accelerating Growth, Secures Major CSP Order — Positive Read-Through for Taiwan Supply Chain
medium.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended a closed-door Morgan Stanley conference, delivering a highly bullish message: quarterly revenue is approaching USD 100 billion, growth momentum is not only intact but accelerating. Notably, Huang disclosed that Nvidia secured a major new order from a large cloud service provider (CSP) that had historically relied primarily on ASIC-based compute — with Nvidia GPU now accounting for nearly 50% of that CSP's compute capacity. This signals continued GPU market share gains over custom ASIC alternatives. Taiwan supply chain beneficiaries highlighted include TSMC, Hon Hai (鴻海), and Quanta (廣達, 2382), as well as Wistron (緯創). Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore described the meeting tone as "constructive." This reaffirms the durability of AI infrastructure investment and is a positive read-through for Taiwan's AI server and advanced packaging supply chain into H2 2026.

medium.title: China Steel (2002) Cuts August Prices Across the Board Amid Seasonal Slowdown
medium.summary:
China Steel (2002) announced August 2026 benchmark prices with hot-rolled, cold-rolled, and galvanized steel all cut by NT$800 per metric ton, following a cumulative reduction of NT$1,100/ton across July and August after six consecutive months of price increases in H1 2026. The cuts reflect typical Q3 seasonal weakness, with reduced demand anticipated from European and American summer slowdowns and the Asian rainy season. Macro headwinds cited include Middle East geopolitical risks pushing oil prices higher, elevated U.S. inflation limiting Fed rate cuts, European rate hikes dampening manufacturing recovery, and sluggish Chinese property market activity. Domestically, Taiwan's economy shows K-shaped recovery — tech sector outperforming while traditional manufacturing lags. Analysts see potential for a Q4 price recovery. **Market Implication:** Near-term pressure on China Steel and downstream steel processors (Yieh Phui, Yu Steel, Sheng Yu Steel, Shin Kong Steel); investors should monitor Q3 earnings guidance and any early signals of Q4 demand recovery.

medium.title: Lite-On Invests US$919 Million to Establish Manufacturing Base in McKinney, Texas
medium.summary: Lite-On Technology (2301) announced that its previously disclosed US investment plan will be headquartered in McKinney, Texas, with total investment of approximately US$919 million, including over US$100 million for facility acquisition. The new manufacturing base — over 650,000 square feet — will support manufacturing, operations, and R&D functions and is expected to create more than 600 jobs, making it one of the largest private investment projects in McKinney's history. The move is strategically aimed at capitalizing on rapid growth in AI infrastructure and energy markets in North America. For investors, this signals Lite-On's commitment to nearshoring and strengthening its North American client relationships amid ongoing supply chain restructuring trends. The scale of investment also reflects growing confidence in long-term AI infrastructure buildout demand.

medium.title: Niche Demand Surge and MLC-to-SLC Migration Drive Forecast 120–170% Price Increase for SLC NAND in H2 2026
medium.summary: TrendForce's latest memory price survey highlights an acute supply shortage in MLC NAND due to capacity being redirected toward high-value 3D NAND products, forcing industrial, automotive, and networking clients to migrate toward SLC NAND. Combined with growing SLC demand from AI edge computing, data centers, and automotive electronics, the supply-demand gap is widening sharply. TrendForce forecasts SLC contract prices will rise 120–170% in H2 2026 versus H1, with potential for further upside. This dynamic is relevant for investors tracking Taiwan's memory and NAND-related supply chain companies, as pricing tailwinds could support earnings revisions for relevant component makers in the second half of the year.

medium.title: Alchip (世芯-KY) June Revenue Surges 84% MoM, Reaching 15-Month High — Q2 Marks Strongest Quarter in Nearly a Year
medium.summary: Alchip Technologies (3661), a leading ASIC design services firm, reported June consolidated revenue of NT$3.572 billion — a 15-month high — up 84.6% MoM and 15.3% YoY. The surge was driven by volume production shipments of a North American cloud service provider's (CSP) 3nm AI accelerator chip. Q2 consolidated revenue reached NT$7.639 billion, up 82.4% QoQ and the highest in four quarters, ending a six-consecutive-quarter declining trend. Institutional analysts indicate that the ramp-up is still in its early stages, with July and August shipment contributions expected to increase further, potentially setting the stage for record full-year revenue. This is a meaningful data point for tracking fabless AI chip demand flowing through TSMC's 3nm node.

medium.title: Innolux (群創) June Revenue Up 5% MoM; Advanced Packaging Pivot Into TGV and RDL Interposer Offers Long-Term Upside
medium.summary: Innolux (3481) posted June consolidated revenue of NT$21.7 billion, up 5.1% MoM and 17.3% YoY, with H1 2026 revenue reaching NT$130.23 billion — a five-year H1 high. Despite the solid revenue print, the stock fell 6.58% on heavy volume (395,022 lots traded), suggesting the market had priced in stronger results. More strategically, analysts are watching Innolux's entry into next-generation advanced packaging through TGV (Through Glass Via) and RDL interposer technologies, leveraging its glass circuit expertise. Institutional forecasts suggest meaningful AI and high-performance computing chip packaging orders could materialize within one to two years, offering a potential re-rating catalyst beyond the traditional display panel business.
